text.en: A cheerful poem describes children playing in the garden on a fine day. They bounce, throw and catch a ball, tug, pull and fly a kite, and run, skip, jump, sway, slide and swing with friends. In this chapter you will learn new action words, use the joining word and, and make a paper bag puppet.

The poem is about children playing in the garden on every fine day. With a ball, they bounce it, throw it and catch it. With a kite, they tug it, pull it and fly it. With friends, they run, skip, jump, sway, slide and swing. Playing outdoors keeps us healthy and happy, but we must be careful so that we do not get hurt.
Bounce means to spring back up after hitting the ground, as a ball does. Throw means to send something through the air with your hand. Sway means to move slowly from side to side, like a branch in the wind. Slide means to move smoothly over a surface, like on a playground slide.
The poem has pairs such as run and skip, jump and sway, and slide and swing. The word and joins two words that go together. Give and take, sing and dance, eat and drink, catch and throw, run and catch are more pairs joined by and. We can think of our own pairs, such as read and write or sit and stand.
Children play many games, and the same game can have a different name in our mother tongue. When playing, we should take turns, play fairly and take care of ourselves and our friends.
You need a paper bag, a pencil, colour pencils or sketch pens, woollen thread and gum. Fold the base of the bag upward and hold it upside down. Draw the upper lip on the flap and the lower lip just below it, then draw a face and colour it. Slide your hand inside and bend your fingers, and the puppet can talk.

You need a paper bag, a pencil, colour pencils or sketch pens, woollen thread and gum.
Fold the base of the bag upward and hold it upside down. Draw the upper lip on the flap and the lower lip just below it, then draw a face and colour it.
Slide your hand inside and bend your fingers, and the puppet can talk.
Think of a ball touching the ground and rising again. Now picture a leaf rocking in the breeze. Choose a different action word for each movement.
The ball bounces and the leaf sways. Bounce is a movement back up, while sway describes a gentle movement from side to side.
Try two actions with your fingers. Move them across the desk without lifting them, then make them spring up. Say slide for the first movement and bounce for the second.
Say, I can clap. I can march. Put the two actions together so you only need to say I can once.

board.text: I can clap. I can march.

text.en: Say, I can clap and march. And joins the actions, and the words I can still go with both.
And can join naming words too. Say, We brought a hoop and a ball. Point out the two things that and joins.
Imagine Asha takes a turn with the hoop and Arun gets the next turn. Tell someone how they take turns, using the word and once.
You could say, Asha rolls the hoop and Arun waits for his turn. Change the sentence to describe what you would do in a game.
Use the paper bag puppet as a speaker. Make it ask a friend to name a safe place for a running game, then let your friend answer in a full sentence.
Give the puppet two actions to say, such as, I can walk and stop. Check that opening the flap makes the mouth move as the words are spoken.
Tell a short story about a game you enjoy. First name the place, then say what you do there, then tell one way to look after your friends.
Listen to a friend's story and repeat one action they used. Then add a different action with and to make your own sentence.

problem.en: Join the words give, take with and.

text.en: Take the two words.
Put the word and between them.
Give and take is the pair.

why.en: The same works for sing and dance.

problem.en: What happens to a kite in the poem?

text.en: The children tug and pull it.
Then they fly it.

why.en: The kite goes up in the sky.

text.en: They do this on each fine day.

why.en: It is a regular happy game.

prompt.en: Tell what the children do with a ball and a kite.

points.en: Children play with a ball, a kite and friends.
Bounce, throw, sway and slide are action words.
The word and joins two words.
A paper bag can be made into a puppet.
